description: The FIXED deployment smoke matrix for a release (engineering standard §11 MUST: 'homepage, every archive, one single per CPT, /en/ pairs, canonical, hreflang, sitemap, 404'). It is deliberately small and stable: a release gate must not change shape between releases, only its recorded result. Rows are relative paths so the same file verifies the LOCAL build (tests/acceptance) and a deployed site (scripts/verify-deploy.py). Per-CPT singles are discovered over the public REST API at run time and checked by scripts/verify-deploy.py, because hard-coding a slug would make the gate rot as soon as content is renamed.

schema.expect_status: integer HTTP status; redirects are asserted unfollowed
schema.expect_contains: strings that MUST appear in the body
schema.expect_absent: strings that MUST NOT appear in the body

rows.note: The Portuguese front page is the canonical entry point of the site and must serve 200 in pt-BR.
The English layer must be reachable at /en/ after a release; a missing language layer is the most common release regression.
Every CPT archive must load in Portuguese and emit a self-canonical link (standard §11 'every archive').
The event archive must load; the event runtime plugin is in the production steady state.
The course-provider directory archive must load.
The unified opportunities directory archive must load.
The sponsor directory archive must load.
The tourism directory archive must load. Lazer is a separate content type and must never render an event calendar.
The native-post archive relabelled 'Blog' must load.
The /en/ pair of the guide archive must serve English with hreflang alternates (standard §11 '/en/ pairs').
The /en/ pair of the event archive must serve English with hreflang alternates.
The /en/ pair of the tourism archive must serve English with hreflang alternates.
The /en/ blog archive is a real English archive since Stage 5 and must serve English.

The XML sitemap must serve after a release (standard §11 'sitemap'). The fragment is deliberately the XML prolog plus the schema namespace, because Jetpack serves a <sitemapindex> pointing at per-post-type sitemaps rather than a bare <urlset>; asserting <urlset> would make the gate red on a healthy site.
robots.txt must keep serving; a missing robots file is a common upload regression.
An unknown Portuguese URL must be a hard 404, not a soft 200 (standard §11 '404').
An unknown English URL must be a hard 404 too; the /en/ layer must not swallow unknown paths.
A legacy English slug must still 301 to its canonical Portuguese URL, proving the redirect layer survived the release.
